newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates stable in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates stable in quiet trade.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were stable in quiet morning trade on Tuesday, Zagreb money market dealers said.
"Demand for both fresh and old loans was somewhat lower today," one dealer said.
Fresh loans totalling 16.5 million kuna were slightly overshot by supply at 20 million. Of this, most were call money loans at a steady 10.5 percent. One smaller 30-day loan was struck at 16 percent.
But dealers said demand put at some 18 million kuna could not be met in full as lenders and borrowers failed to agree on terms.
Overnight trade totalled 50 million kuna on Monday as one bank made borrowings to maintain its mandatory reserve. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
